title: Abdominal-X-ray network classifies recorded colorectal-cancer status
summary: A DenseNet-121 analyzed abdominal X-rays against recorded colorectal-cancer labels in Taiwanese hospital data. It achieved AUC 0.738 in 16,875 internal-validation patients and 0.656 in 15,876 patients from a community hospital; external sensitivity was 47.7% at the selected cutoff. Cancer was uncommon, registry records could miss diagnoses elsewhere, and the one-year follow-up/label timing limits claims about detection at the image date. This retrospective study does not establish effective screening or earlier diagnosis.
organization: Tri-Service General Hospital; National Defense Medical Center

source_review.scope: Primary relevant cohort/label, DenseNet operation and threshold Methods, validation Results and limitations; supplementary architecture/training appendix not independently read. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Patient-separated development, tuning and validation cohorts, one randomly selected KUB radiograph per person, and registry/EMR colorectal-cancer labels. The threshold chosen in the tuning set was reused in both validation cohorts; external AUC .656 and sensitivity 47.7% were lower than internal results.
evidence.unknown: Prospective screening performance, time gained before diagnosis and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Prior cancer was excluded and one-year follow-up used, but the precise diagnosis-to-image timing is not fully specified. Low case prevalence, distal-tumor imbalance and incomplete capture of outside-hospital diagnoses limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: A 121-layer DenseNet learns radiographic patterns associated with recorded colorectal-cancer labels and returns a case probability for a single abdominal radiograph.
